St. Jacob Netsvetov

St. Jacob Netsvetov

Period

Region

Titles / vocation
Priest · Missionary
Commemoration

Introduction

St. Jacob Netsvetov is remembered as a missionary priest of Alaska with Russian and Aleut family roots. The OCA life describes his education, family, pastoral travels, translation, and ministry under difficult conditions. His record gives the Saints section a connection with Indigenous North American Christian history. Miraculous and devotional elements remain attributed to the complete published account.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Jacob was born on Atka in 1802 to a Russian father and an Aleut mother. He studied at Irkutsk, married Anna, and was ordained.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “1802”

Life and notable events

Long journeys marked his Alaskan ministry. After his wife’s death, a fire, and his father’s death, he continued missionary service, eventually leading the Kvikhpak mission.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “Kvikhpak”

Death and martyrdom

After accusations, he was summoned to Sitka and cleared. His health declined, and he died there on July 26, 1864.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “1864”

Writings and legacy

His journals record local travel and pastoral work among Alaska’s Indigenous peoples.

[1] Ecclesiastical saint’s life · Published life; biographical narrative, source anchor “journal”

The OCA resource distinguishes his birth on Atka, death in Sitka, and the later glorification services of October 15–16,1994. The latter services mark the formal recognition of his sainthood.

[2] Ecclesiastical history or testimony · OCA Feasts and Saints resource; biographical and glorification dates
